Based on Fx Product Manager feedback, we're factoring an alternative to autosaving pages during the setup process: a warning popup that prompts the user to save if they're trying to navigate to another page and hadn't saved yet. 

Expected behavior A: User then saves and moves onto next page.

Expected behavior B: User doesn't want to save latest changes - selects "Continue Anyway" button or something of the sort to proceed.

I absolutely expect us to integrate an AI assistant at some point, we're in the process of barely prototyping that now, and I suspect it will take us some time of experimentation with a basic assistant before we can start thinking about how to embed/integrate it into the application and workflow more richly like this.  I'd move this out to a post-mvp phase, but I do expect it to come at some point.

This idea of dragging/dropping sections into an experiment is another thing that's been growing in my head for a while that I'm happy to see shown here.  I can imagine a user adding branches to their experiment this way, or adding features, or adding audiences.

Ie if you create an experiment from scratch (not a template) this page might be a bit barebones, and then you start building the experiment up by adding relevant sections (features, branches, audiences, metrics, etc) until it becomes the full experiment.  I love that idea.

Expanding sections into more detail is exactly what I was hoping for, so we don't end up with the very very old pattern of 'static form page, static detail page'.  We're not locked into that kind of pattern, we can build pages dynamically like this, so let's absolutely take advantage of that and make a smoother experience for the user.

+++++ I love this, this is, is exactly what I was hoping for.

You can see the overview of the experiment at a glance.

You can drill into sections for more detail.

You can see how far through the process you are.

You can clearly see which parts are done, and what's left to do.

And you can comment/discuss things.

Only thing missing here is the review/launch/monitor/end(results) parts but I think they should slot into this general pattern pretty nicely.

I love it!
+1 to template previews, also we could track experiments/rollouts that are derived from templates and show like, links or screenshots or something here as 'Examples: [1, 2, 3, ...]'

The idea of having a branching questionaire that leads you towards some more specific template or prefilled fields is a good idea, but I've built this kind of thing before and it winds up being a lot of complexity you don't originally realize or intend.  You can get some of the same effect with the menu of templates below but avoid a lot of the complexity from having to manage the relationships between questions/answers/branches/etc.

If the idea here is we actually parse the answer to the question to help figure out what steps to do next, that probably lumps together with the AI agent approach down below, which I do think is a thing we will do but probably not immediately, I'd treat that as a followup to this UI rewrite.

I like the idea that users can have their own internal set of templates, I think users are essentially already doing this now so making it a more first class workflow probably makes sense and shouldn't be very complicated.

I really like the idea of having previews like this, actually this is kind of already built using about:messagepreview so I think we'd just have to find some way to hook it in with experimenter.  Should be doable but I might consider this like a post-mvp idea.

+1 This idea of having entry points to building blank experiments/rollouts/labs, but also a selection of templates, I think is both approachable from an engineering perspective, and also the direction we've gotten a lot of feedback in the past about having a menu of simple prebuilt options.
Karen's top choice for structure - I believe this is one of the most easily adoptable flow for a wider audience.

* add saved templates
